A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same quantization study. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite the added reasoning evaluation and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization accuracy, output-similarity, latency, throughput, and cost measurements in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original DeepSeek-R1-Distill reasoning evaluations in Section 4.3 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The quantization procedures in Section 3.2 remain unchanged, including RTN for FP8, GPTQ and activation quantization for INT8, and GPTQ with MSE-optimal clipping for INT4. Testing distilled models introduces no reported new quantization component or training procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on AIME 2024, MATH-500, and GPQA-Diamond. These extend existing mathematics and reasoning coverage, which already included MATH Level 5 and GPQA, while retaining all earlier academic, coding, chat, and long-context benchmarks.

E2.justification: GPTQ and AWQ participation in Table 1 and Appendix A.2 is unchanged. The added reasoning benchmarks use the existing BF16, W8A8-FP, W8A8-INT, and W4A16-INT comparison set rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: The added study substantially expands the evaluated model configurations to DeepSeek-R1-Distill Llama-8B/70B and Qwen-1.5B/7B/14B/32B. It introduces LightEval pass@1 evaluations using temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95. These are new experimental settings; the earlier Llama-3.1 and inference-performance protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The output-similarity investigation and latency-throughput case studies are retained unchanged. The reasoning addition supplies benchmark evaluations, without a separate new ablation, robustness intervention, sensitivity analysis, or error study.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 specifies 20 sampled responses per query for estimating reasoning pass@1, and Table 4 introduces corresponding ± values without defining their statistical meaning. The existing two-run Arena-Hard results and 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged; this is not evidence of increased runs for those experiments.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds a substantial body of results for previously unevaluated distilled reasoning models. Reported average accuracy recovery ranges from 99.0–101.0% for FP8, while Qwen-1.5B recovers 96.9% with INT8 and 93.5% with INT4. Earlier numerical results and all six figures, including appendix results, are unchanged; these are new-setting outcomes.

T1.justification: The RTN definition, Equation (1), and associated mathematical discussion are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added; the new pass@1 evaluation introduces no formal mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory findings, and conclusion retain the same accuracy, GPTQ-versus-AWQ, and deployment-efficiency claims. The reasoning results add supporting evidence without revising those main contribution statements.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets the earlier accuracy conclusions as extending to distilled reasoning models, describing larger losses for small INT4 models as reasonable. Its >99% recovery summary does not fully acknowledge other exceptions, such as Qwen-1.5B INT8 at 96.9%. Earlier explanations and the limitations section are unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies and links LightEval and supplies generation parameters and the response count for the added reasoning evaluation. Existing calibration, quantization, vLLM, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. The addition does not document model-specific calibration choices or how its ± values were calculated.

R1.justification: The reasoning section adds citations to DeepSeek-R1, LightEval, and Lightman et al. The additional 2024 GPQA reference represents the same work already cited as Rein et al. (2023). The related-work discussion and positioning against prior quantization studies remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts Section 4.3, renumbers Text Similarity Investigation to 4.4, shortens the Section 4.2 heading, and adds an accent to an author's name. Existing prose and the overall narrative structure are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a full-width reasoning-results table. Former Tables 4–12 become Tables 5–13, with accompanying page reflow and modest repositioning of existing material. The six figures and retained table designs are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 4 extend the previously Llama-3.1-only evidence to distilled reasoning models, including Qwen, and expose larger losses in small integer-quantized models. This improves the study's empirical usefulness while preserving earlier evidence. Undefined ± statistics and an overly broad >99% recovery summary limit the strength of the addition, but do not outweigh its value.
